heading.en: Why does a battery run down?

hook.en: A new cell and an old cell have the same chemicals, but the old one gives less voltage. The voltage depends on concentration, and the *Nernst equation* tells us how.
hook.kn: ಹೊಸ ಮತ್ತು ಹಳೆಯ ಕೋಶಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ರಾಸಾಯನಿಕಗಳಿದ್ದರೂ ಹಳೆಯದು ಕಡಿಮೆ ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ಸಾರತೆಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸಿದೆ; ನರ್ನ್ಸ್ಟ್ ಸಮೀಕರಣ ಅದನ್ನು ತಿಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Apply the Nernst equation to electrodes and cells
Relate E°cell to ΔG° and to K

say.en: A new cell and an old cell have the same chemicals, but the old one gives less voltage. The voltage depends on concentration, and the Nernst equation tells us how. In this lesson: Apply the Nernst equation to electrodes and cells.
Relate E degreescell to delta G degrees and to K.

body.en: For a cell reaction aA + bB → cC + dD involving n electrons, $E_{cell} = E^\circ_{cell} - \frac{2.303RT}{nF}\log Q$. At 298 K, 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V. For the Daniell cell, $E = 1.1 - \frac{0.059}{2}\log\frac{[Zn^{2+}]}{[Cu^{2+}]}$. Pure solids are left out of Q. As the cell runs, products build up, Q rises and the emf falls; at *equilibrium* E = 0.
body.kn: n ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನುಗಳು ಭಾಗವಹಿಸುವ ಕ್ರಿಯೆಗೆ 298 K ನಲ್ಲಿ E = E° − (0.059/n) log Q. ಕೋಶ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡಿದಂತೆ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿ ವೋಲ್ಟೇಜ್ ಇಳಿಯುತ್ತದೆ; ಸಮತೋಲನದಲ್ಲಿ E ಶೂನ್ಯ.

title.en: On the board: the Nernst equation

say.en: The cell e.m.f. depends on concentrations. At 298 K the Nernst equation is E equals E zero minus 0.059 over n log Q.
For the Daniell cell n is 2 and Q is zinc ion over copper ion concentration.
Gibbs energy and the equilibrium constant follow from E zero.
E against log Q is a straight line with slope minus 0.059 over n. When Q is 1, E equals E zero.
For the Daniell cell: delta G zero is about minus 212 kilojoules, and log K is 37.3, so K is about 2 times ten to the 37.
On the board: the Nernst equation.

title.en: Nernst equation for the Daniell cell

narration.en: E = E° − (2.303RT/2F) log([Zn²⁺]/[Cu²⁺]), with E° = 1.10 V. Making [Cu²⁺] larger or [Zn²⁺] smaller raises E. ΔG = −nFE, and at equilibrium E = 0, which gives log K = 2E°/0.059 at 298 K.

body.en: The maximum electrical work a cell can do is nFE, so $\Delta G = -nFE_{cell}$ and $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{cell}$. A positive E° means a negative ΔG°: the reaction is spontaneous. At *equilibrium* E = 0, which gives $E^\circ_{cell} = \frac{0.059}{n}\log K_c$ at 298 K. Since ΔG° = −2.303RT log K, all three quantities are linked.
body.kn: ΔG° = −nFE°; ಧನ E° ಎಂದರೆ ಋಣ ΔG°, ಅಂದರೆ ಸ್ವಯಂಪ್ರೇರಿತ ಕ್ರಿಯೆ. ಸಮತೋಲನದಲ್ಲಿ E° = (0.059/n) log K.

narration.en: The maximum electrical work a cell can do is n F E, so delta G equals minus n F E cell. A positive E zero means a negative delta G zero: the reaction is spontaneous. At equilibrium E is zero, which gives E zero cell equals 0.059 by n, times log K c, at 298 kelvin.
narration.kn: ΔG° = −nFE°; ಧನ E° ಎಂದರೆ ಋಣ ΔG°, ಅಂದರೆ ಸ್ವಯಂಪ್ರೇರಿತ ಕ್ರಿಯೆ. ಸಮತೋಲನದಲ್ಲಿ E° = (0.059/n) log K.

say.en: The maximum electrical work a cell can do is n F E, so delta G equals minus n F E cell. A positive E zero means a negative delta G zero: the reaction is spontaneous. At equilibrium E is zero, which gives E zero cell equals 0.059 by n, times log K c, at 298 kelvin. F equals 96487 C mol to the power minus 1 is approximately 96500 C mol to the power minus 1.
say.kn: delta G degrees equals -nFE degrees; ಧನ E degrees ಎಂದರೆ ಋಣ delta G degrees, ಅಂದರೆ ಸ್ವಯಂಪ್ರೇರಿತ ಕ್ರಿಯೆ. ಸಮತೋಲನದಲ್ಲಿ E degrees equals (0.059 over n) log K.

problem.en: Find the emf at 298 K of Zn | Zn²⁺(0.1 M) || Cu²⁺(1 M) | Cu, given E°cell = 1.10 V.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the emf at 298 K of Zn | Zn²⁺(0.1 M) || Cu²⁺(1 M) | Cu, given E°cell = 1.10 V.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the emf at 298 kelvin of Zn | Zn squared⁺0.1 M || Cu squared⁺1 M | Cu, given E degreescell equals 1.10 volts.
Zn plus Cu squared⁺ gives Zn squared⁺ plus Cu, n equals 2, Q = [Zn squared⁺]/[Cu squared⁺] = 0.1 over 1 equals 0.1.
E equals 1.10 - (0.059 over 2) log 0.1 equals 1.10 minus 0.0295 times minus 1.
E equals 1.10 plus 0.0295 equals 1.1295 volts.
So the answer is is approximately 1.13 volts.

problem.en: For Cu(s) + 2Ag⁺(aq) → Cu²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s), E°cell = 0.46 V. Find ΔG° and Kc at 298 K.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. For Cu(s) + 2Ag⁺(aq) → Cu²⁺(aq) + 2Ag(s), E°cell = 0.46 V. Find ΔG° and Kc at 298 K.

say.en: Let us solve this together. For Cus plus 2Ag⁺aq gives Cu squared⁺aq plus 2Ags, E degreescell equals 0.46 volts. Find delta G degrees and Kc at 298 kelvin.

n equals 2. delta G degrees equals -nFE degrees equals minus 2 times 96500 times 0.46 equals minus 88 780 joules mol to the power minus 1 is approximately minus 88.8 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1.
log Kc equals nE degrees/0.059 equals 2 times 0.46 over 0.059 equals 15.59.
Kc equals antilog 15.59 is approximately 3.9 times 10 to the power 15.
So the answer is delta G degrees is approximately minus 88.8 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1; Kc is approximately 3.9 times 10 to the power 15.
